claims.title: Ancient peopling of the land
claims.summary: Hunting and gathering peoples settle the long territory between the Andes and the Pacific over many millennia, the deep ancestors of the Mapuche and the Andean peoples of the north.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-10000bce-ancient-peopling-of-the-land, claim TL:CHL:event:10000bce:ancient-peopling-of-the-land, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The moai of Rapa Nui
claims.summary: On Easter Island, the Polynesian society of Rapa Nui carves and raises some 900 colossal stone moai on hundreds of ceremonial platforms, an unrivalled monumental tradition later recognised by UNESCO.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1000-the-moai-of-rapa-nui, claim TL:CHL:event:1000:the-moai-of-rapa-nui, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Inca expansion reaches the Maule
claims.summary: The Inca empire extends its influence into northern and central Chile but is unable to subdue the Mapuche, whose resistance checks imperial control near the Maule River.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1470-inca-expansion-reaches-the-maule, claim TL:CHL:event:1470:inca-expansion-reaches-the-maule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Almagro's expedition turns back
claims.summary: Diego de Almagro leads the first Spanish entry into Chile as far as the Maule River; finding no gold or empire, the expedition returns to Peru, but the Spanish first clash with the Araucanians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1536-almagro-s-expedition-turns-back, claim TL:CHL:event:1536:almagro-s-expedition-turns-back, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Santiago
claims.summary: Pedro de Valdivia founds Santiago de Nueva Extremadura in the central valley, the nucleus of Spanish Chile and its future capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1541-founding-of-santiago, claim TL:CHL:event:1541:founding-of-santiago, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest reaches the Biobio
claims.summary: Valdivia extends Spanish rule south of the Biobio and founds Concepcion, pushing into the Mapuche heartland and igniting lasting resistance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1550-conquest-reaches-the-biobio, claim TL:CHL:event:1550:conquest-reaches-the-biobio, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mapuche defeat and kill Valdivia
claims.summary: At Tucapel, Mapuche forces led by Lautaro destroy a Spanish column and capture Valdivia, who is executed; the disaster opens the long Arauco War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1553-mapuche-defeat-and-kill-valdivia, claim TL:CHL:event:1553:mapuche-defeat-and-kill-valdivia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The frontier Captaincy General
claims.summary: Chile is governed as a poor, militarised captaincy general of the Spanish empire, its southern frontier held against an independent Mapuche nation that the conquest never subdued.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1600-the-frontier-captaincy-general, claim TL:CHL:event:1600:the-frontier-captaincy-general, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First national junta
claims.summary: Creole leaders in Santiago form a governing junta after the fall of the Spanish king, the founding act of Chilean self-government and the national day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1810-first-national-junta, claim TL:CHL:event:1810:first-national-junta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Crossing the Andes and Chacabuco
claims.summary: San Martin's Army of the Andes crosses the cordillera and defeats the royalists at Chacabuco, opening the road to Santiago and the liberation of Chile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1817-crossing-the-andes-and-chacabuco, claim TL:CHL:event:1817:crossing-the-andes-and-chacabuco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Battle of Maipu
claims.summary: Patriot forces under San Martin, with O'Higgins, crush the Spanish royalists near Santiago, sealing Chilean independence on the mainland weeks after its formal declaration.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1818-the-battle-of-maipu, claim TL:CHL:event:1818:the-battle-of-maipu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Constitution of 1833
claims.summary: A conservative constitution shaped by Diego Portales establishes a strong centralised presidency, anchoring decades of unusual political stability.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1833-the-constitution-of-1833, claim TL:CHL:event:1833:the-constitution-of-1833, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The War of the Pacific
claims.summary: A dispute over nitrate taxes leads Chile to war with Peru and Bolivia; Chilean victories win the nitrate-rich Atacama and leave Bolivia landlocked.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1879-the-war-of-the-pacific, claim TL:CHL:event:1879:the-war-of-the-pacific, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pacification of Araucania
claims.summary: After three centuries of independence, the Chilean state subdues the Mapuche south of the Biobio by military campaign and opens their territory to settlement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1881-pacification-of-araucania, claim TL:CHL:event:1881:pacification-of-araucania, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Neruda wins the Nobel Prize
claims.summary: Pablo Neruda, poet, diplomat and senator, is awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, crowning Chile's golden age of letters.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1971-neruda-wins-the-nobel-prize, claim TL:CHL:event:1971:neruda-wins-the-nobel-prize, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Election of Salvador Allende
claims.summary: The Marxist Salvador Allende of the Popular Unity coalition wins a narrow plurality and is confirmed by Congress, the first freely elected Marxist head of state in the Americas.

sources.label: The Allende Years and the Pinochet Coup, 1969-1973
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1970-election-of-salvador-allende, claim TL:CHL:event:1970:election-of-salvador-allende, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The military coup
claims.summary: The armed forces under General Augusto Pinochet overthrow President Salvador Allende, who dies as troops storm La Moneda, ending Chile's democratic experiment.

sources.label: The Allende Years and the Pinochet Coup, 1969-1973
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Pinochet dictatorship
claims.summary: Pinochet's regime represses opponents through detention, torture, killing and forced disappearance while imposing free-market reforms; the abuses are later documented by the Rettig and Valech commissions.

sources.label: Truth Commission: Chile (National Commission on Truth and Reconciliation, Rettig report)
Commission of Inquiry: Chile (National Commission on Political Imprisonment and Torture, Valech report)

claims.title: The 1980 Constitution
claims.summary: A constitution drafted under the dictatorship is approved in a controlled plebiscite, entrenching military prerogatives and remaining, much amended, in force for decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1980-the-1980-constitution, claim TL:CHL:event:1980:the-1980-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 'No' plebiscite
claims.summary: Asked to extend Pinochet's rule, Chileans vote No by 55 to 43 percent, compelling the open presidential election that opens the path back to democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1988-the-no-plebiscite, claim TL:CHL:event:1988:the-no-plebiscite, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to democracy
claims.summary: Patricio Aylwin is inaugurated president, restoring civilian democratic rule and soon creating the Rettig Commission to investigate the dictatorship's crimes.

sources.label: Truth Commission: Chile (National Commission on Truth and Reconciliation, Rettig report)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1990-return-to-democracy, claim TL:CHL:event:1990:return-to-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Pinochet arrested in London
claims.summary: Augusto Pinochet is detained in London on a foreign warrant for human-rights crimes, a landmark in the pursuit of accountability before his death in 2006.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-1998-pinochet-arrested-in-london, claim TL:CHL:event:1998:pinochet-arrested-in-london, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 'estallido social' protests
claims.summary: A metro fare rise in Santiago ignites the largest protests since the dictatorship, broadening into demands for reform of pensions, health, education and the constitution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-2019-the-estallido-social-protests, claim TL:CHL:event:2019:the-estallido-social-protests, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: New constitution rejected
claims.summary: After a 2020 vote to rewrite the charter, Chileans reject a sweeping progressive draft 62 to 38 percent, a major blow to President Gabriel Boric; a later attempt also fails.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chile: From the Mapuche of the south and the moai-builders of Rapa Nui to the Spanish founding of Santiago in 1541, the independence sealed at Maipu in 1818, the nitrate wealth of the War of the Pacific, the rupture of 1973, the Pinochet dictatorship and the long democratic recovery.", terralore.co/country/CHL/chronicle#ev-2022-new-constitution-rejected, claim TL:CHL:event:2022:new-constitution-rejected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
